habit_scope: Not a competing foundation type. Sequence step on CIP/CMU basement (and below-grade crawl faces).
how_it_is_done: After the CIP or CMU wall stands: CIP plug form-tie holes; CMU parge first (ORNL checklist; AF&PA Concrete Foundations; ORNL notes 6, 22, 31, 33).
Choose dampproof + poly for vapor vs waterproof if finished basement, poor drainage, water history, or hydrostatic (ORNL BFH §2.2). This is a detailing choice, not a foundation-type winner.
Waterproof on the wall; insulation outboard of it; down to the footing drain (ORNL note 6).
Protection board on exterior foam to 6 in below grade (ORNL note 1).
Drain tile at the CIP/CMU footing (ORNL note 8; AF&PA drain tile around entire CIP/block footing). Tile is NOT used with PWF (D9) — do not shop tile onto m-P05-pwf.
Finish this work before backfill. Waterproofing PRECEDES backfill (ORNL note 1 / §2.2). can_overlap false on that hold.
Do not trade soil treatment for termite shields (D8 / c-P05-D8-termite-shields). Shields optional and not sufficient alone (ORNL).
trades: construction contractor (ORNL checklist) — no crew size
tools_equipment: Not a tool list in sources.
inspection_hold_points: Form-tie holes plugged / CMU parged before coating (ORNL).
Waterproofing (or dampproofing as chosen) in place before backfill (ORNL note 1).
Protection board on exterior foam to 6 in below grade (ORNL note 1).
Drain tile laid holes-down, gravel, fabric, outfall or sump, not tied to roof leaders (ORNL note 8) — CIP/CMU only.
when_this_beats_habit: Not a type habit. Waterproof beats dampproof when the basement will be finished, drainage is poor, or hydrostatic is in play (ORNL §2.2). Dampproof + poly is the vapor-only path.
when_this_is_a_bad_idea: Do not coat then backfill without protection board on exterior foam. Do not put drain tile on PWF. Do not skip this step on a below-grade basement wall. SOG above grade typically needs neither subdrain nor waterproofing (ORNL Ch 4).
why_tier1_never_learned_it: They learned dampproof. Waterproof vs dampproof is the detailing fork they skip until a wet basement teaches them.
permit_gate: should be on drawings before permit
permit_gate_notes: Finished-basement waterproof vs dampproof should show on drawings. Not a P08 item.
risk_if_swapped_late: You cannot swap dampproof for waterproof after backfill without digging the walls back out.
plain_language_summary: This is not a foundation type. After the wall is up, coat it before you backfill. Dampproof if you only need vapor; waterproof if the basement will be lived in or the site is wet. Drain tile at the footing for poured or block walls — not for the wood foundation. Protection board over the foam so the backfill does not rip it.
spanish_summary: Esto no es un tipo de cimiento. Cuando la pared ya está, se cubre antes de rellenar. Dampproof si solo es vapor; impermeabilizar si el sótano se va a habitar o el terreno es mojado. Tubo de drenaje en zapata de concreto o block, no en cimiento de madera. Tabla de protección sobre el foam.

layering: CMU: parge, then dampproof/asphalt (AF&PA). CIP: plug form-tie holes before waterproofing (ORNL).
Waterproof on the wall, insulation outboard of it, down to the footing drain (ORNL note 6).
Protection board on exterior foam to 6 in below grade (ORNL note 1).
Drain tile: 4-in perf, holes down, 1 in in 20 ft (ORNL note 8). NOT PWF (D9).
Manufacturer video CLASS: dimple drain membrane / drain tile (not Platon brand; not CIP dampproof-asphalt habit).
code_to_check: No named IRC R-number for dampproof vs waterproof in this set. Confirm with AHJ / engineer (gap-sop-irc-section-numbers).
time_money: Waterproof vs dampproof is a basement detailing choice before backfill; you cannot swap after the dirt is in. Drain tile is not a PWF skip. No dollars in sources.
